beats.text: Current video models waste massive compute trying to generate high-res pixels before they even understand the basic semantic structure of the scene they are building.
beats.visual_focus: A chaotic pixel-cloud flickering rapidly on a black screen.

beats.text: It’s like a sketch artist trying to paint a masterpiece by obsessing over individual brush hairs before they’ve even drawn the outline of the subject.
beats.visual_focus: A charcoal pencil drawing an outline, then suddenly zooming into microscopic hair fibers.

beats.text: SemanTok fixes this by injecting frozen DINO features into the tokenizer, forcing the model to reconstruct global semantics from the very first token prefix.
beats.visual_focus: A DINO feature map overlaying a latent space, snapping tokens into a coherent semantic grid.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook is solid—I hate waiting for models to render garbage, so calling out pixel-first waste is a win. The sketch artist analogy in Beat 2 actually works because it's not condescending. I got a bit lost on 'frozen DINO features'—I know DINO is a vision transformer, but just saying 'frozen' might trip up people who haven't touched self-supervised learning papers. Still, it's way better than the usual 'AI magic' fluff I see on my feed.
